headline: Netwealth CEO acknowledges Hub24 as a strong competitor but says both are taking share from legacy platforms
reasoning: Matt Heine acknowledges Hub24 as a compelling and strong competitor, noting that together Hub24 and Netwealth capture around 80% of gross flows into the platform market. Both were the only two platforms in the industry to grow market share in the 12 months to March, with all legacy platforms either holding steady or going backwards. He notes each platform has differentiated features attractive to advisors, and views competition as healthy for driving industry improvement.
quote: they're clearly a very good competitor. And between the two of us, we currently receive around 80% of all grossing flows into the platform market. So we're both growing very quickly. We're both increasing our market share. And in fact, for the financial year, throughout the 12 months to March, um, hub and net wealth were actually the only two platforms in the industry to grow their market share. All of the others, the legacy platforms and whatnot, either stayed steady or went backwards.
episode_title: Netwealth eyeing a bigger slice of the wealth management boom

headline: Netwealth CEO Matt Heine bullish on long-term growth, targeting doubled FUA by 2030 despite First Guardian remediation costs
reasoning: Netwealth delivered record FY26 revenue of $391 million, up 20%, with underlying profit (ex-First Guardian costs) rising 16%, though statutory NPAT fell 48% due to $105 million in legal remediation costs. The company has guided to $18–20 billion in net inflows for FY27 with a 47% EBITDA margin, and has an ambition (not a formal forecast) to double funds under administration by 2030. Heine emphasised the total addressable market is significantly larger than just the platform market, with Netwealth currently holding only around 2% share. He noted the business is on a 'rule of 40' basis the second most efficient stock on the ASX, and the margin compression from 49% to 47% EBITDA is deliberate investment for future growth. Key growth segments include affluent advice, high net worth, ultra high net worth, and broking.
quote: The market is significantly bigger than just a platform market, which is what many of our investors tend to focus on. And in our results we've actually looked to detail our total addressable market, which we believe is very significant, of which we currently only have about 2%. So we remain bullish on the future. We've got incredibly strong tailwinds. But equally we do need to recognize that, you know, there are always risks and that could be a macroeconomic risk or something else that we haven't seen. But as it stands, very confident.
episode_title: Netwealth eyeing a bigger slice of the wealth management boom

headline: Netwealth's AI assistant Nova answering 15-19% of all chat inquiries within first month of launch, with broader AI-driven efficiency gains expected across engineering and product teams.
reasoning: Matt Heine highlights that Netwealth's generative AI virtual assistant, Nova, was handling 15-19% of all inbound chat inquiries within its first month of going live, and will continue to improve over time. Beyond customer-facing AI, Heine notes significant upside from automating internal processes including data extraction and data management. He believes AI capability within Netwealth's engineering and product teams could deliver up to 30% efficiency gains over the next 12-24 months. These gains could manifest as headcount flatness, cost savings passed on to customers, or faster delivery of new technology features.
quote: within the first month of going live, Nova was answering in the vicinity of 15 to 19% of all income inquiries through the chat channels. That was a really good enhancement, one that will keep building out and ensuring they get smarter over time. Um, equally, uh, being an administration and technology business, a lot of upsides just around automating, um, processes, data extraction, data management and where we're seeing very significant opportunity. And a really big upside is within our engineering and product teams. So using all of the AI capability to make sure that we can deliver more capability much faster at a high quality. And we think that, you know, there's no reason over the next 12 to 24 months, we shouldn't be able to gain up to sort of 30% efficiency in that team. So, uh, that can then play out in a whole range of ways, whether it's actually, um, sort of flattening out headcount in the future, passing back extra revenue as savings to our customers or just delivering fantastic new tech.
episode_title: Netwealth eyeing a bigger slice of the wealth management boom

The firm is investing in technology, products, and new segments (high net worth, ultra high net worth, broking) to accelerate its strategy, reflecting confidence in long-term structural demand for managed platform services in Australia.

headline: Netwealth CEO sees massive structural tailwind as 3.5–5 million Australians seek advice against a backdrop of only 10–12,000 advisors
reasoning: Matt Heine identifies a significant supply-demand imbalance in Australian financial advice: an estimated 3.5 to 5 million Australians are expected to seek advice over the next 5 to 10 years, yet only 10,000 to 12,000 advisors exist to service them. This structural gap is a core growth driver for platform businesses like Netwealth, which are investing in technology to help advisors scale from roughly 120 clients to 150–200 clients without degrading advice quality. The ability to help advisors become more efficient is framed as both a commercial opportunity and a social impact theme for Netwealth.
quote: there is a huge supply and demand issue and gap in the Australian market at the moment. We believe that there's somewhere in the vicinity of three and a half to 5 million Australians that will be seeking advice in the next 5 to 10 years, and only 10 to 12,000 advisors to actually service them. So you can see that there's a real mismatch in that supply and demand equation. So our real focus is how do we help advisors deliver better advice to more Australians.
episode_title: Netwealth eyeing a bigger slice of the wealth management boom
